what_it_is.prose: Dassault Aviation SA is a French aerospace and defence company headquartered in Saint-Cloud, France, and the manufacturer of the Rafale multi-role fighter and the Mirage 2000. Dassault has a longstanding relationship with the Indian Air Force, having supplied the original Mirage 2000H (51 aircraft, inducted 1985-2007) and more recently the Rafale (36 aircraft, delivered 2020-2022 under a EUR 7.87 billion inter-governmental agreement signed in 2016). Dassault is a leading contender for India's ₹1.5 lakh crore+ Multi-Role Fighter Aircraft (MRFA) programme to procure 114 fighters, with the Rafale Marine (F4/R standard, naval variant for the Indian Navy's future aircraft carriers) as its offering. Dassault also maintains India's existing Mirage 2000 fleet through an ongoing upgrade programme, including a new radar, cockpit avionics, and the Meteor beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile. Dassault's global order backlog stands at approximately EUR 45 billion as of end 2025, providing strong production continuity.

faq.question: What is Dassault Aviation's relationship with India?
faq.answer: Dassault has supplied India with 51 Mirage 2000H fighters (1985-2007) and 36 Rafale fighters (2020-2022). The 36 Rafale were delivered under a EUR 7.87 billion inter-governmental agreement signed in 2016. Dassault also maintains the Indian Mirage 2000 fleet through an upgrade programme and is a leading contender for the ₹1.5 lakh crore+ MRFA programme with the Rafale Marine.

faq.question: What is the MRFA competition?
faq.answer: The Multi-Role Fighter Aircraft (MRFA) programme is India's bid to procure 114 fighters for the Indian Air Force and Navy at an estimated cost of ₹1.5 lakh crore+. Dassault Aviation's Rafale Marine (naval variant) is a leading contender, competing against Boeing's F/A-18E/F Super Hornet and others. The Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) was granted in 2026, but the competitive evaluation and contract award is expected to take 2-3 more years.

faq.question: Can India produce Rafale fighters domestically?
faq.answer: Dassault has offered to set up a final assembly line in India for Rafale MRFA aircraft under a Strategic Partnership (SP) model with an Indian partner. Whether Dassault will offer full Transfer of Technology for local manufacturing, or only final assembly from imported kits, remains a key question for the MRFA competition. The earlier 36-aircraft order was an off-the-shelf import.
